notes: Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency personalization + batch reranking. Primary drivers: predictable throughput, p99 latency SLOs, predictable unit economics for RTB-like traffic.
Initial ask from infra lead (Angus): reserve 16 GPUs (A100-class) with ability to burst to 32 for 10% of traffic windows. Wants concrete throughput guarantees per-GPU for our model mix.

Workload profile: daytime spikes (09:00-11:00, 15:00-16:30 PT), median request qps ~1.2k, peak sustained 6k qps for 20-40 min. Typical seq len median 96 tokens, 90th perc 512 tokens. Mix = 60% rerank, 25% embeddings, 15% chat-like generate.
Latency targets: p95 <= 60ms for embeddings/rerank (online path), p99 <= 250ms for chat/generation (soft); infra asks for strict p99 <= 200ms on dedicated for contract negotiation.
POC results (see drive csv): continuous load test 48h w/ reserved 16 GPUs: avg p95 embeddings 55ms, p99 embeddings 120ms; p99 chat spiked to 320ms during cold-start events.

Autoscaling notes from SE review (Riley): default scale-up policy causes 45-60s ramp to add GPU nodes from cold; need warm pool strategy to get sub-10s effective capacity. Redwood suggests warm pool of 2-4 pre-warmed workers per AZ.

Queueing behavior: under burst, our current app queues requests at ingress for up to 6s before backend rejects; prefer graceful queueing with backpressure + early-fail thresholds. Ask: configurable queue length + per-route queuing SLOs.

Warm pools details discussed: pre-warm cache (LLM KV cold) vs pre-warm worker with model loaded. Magnetar wants both: keep model loaded on warm workers for recent variants, maintain shared KV cache to reduce token generation work.

Scale-down policy: current POC shows aggressive scale-down (5 min idle) causes frequent churn during traffic oscillation; recommend 15-30m cooldown with predictive scale-down using traffic windows (cron + smoothing). Customer prefers hysteresis to avoid cold penalties.
Warm-up costs: finance flagged ~10% run-rate uplift for warm pools; expected to be offset by fewer cold-start misses and lower p99 SLAs penalties. Need modeling for net unit cost.

SLA negotiation points: uptime SLA 99.95% target; p99 latency crediting model requested (credits when p99 > threshold for >15m). Legal asks for defined measurement windows and exclusion for scheduled maintenance.
Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to smaller quantized model in case of capacity shortages; require policy controls for per-route fallback and automatic warm-up of fallback path.
KV cache and prefix caching: magnets want transparent prefix/KV caching across requests to maintain low latency for repeated candidates — ask for cache hit metrics in console and TTL controls.
Operational transparency needed: token-level cost breakdown, per-GPU throughput charts, queue length time series, and warm pool metrics. These will be part of the SLA appendix.
Security: VPC peering + SAML SSO for console, HSM/KMS for keys, audit logs retention 1 year. Legal flagged cross-region data residency for EU users (must restrict to eu-1 region for EU traffic).

Internal stakeholders: CTO (Lena Ortiz) cares about unit economics; Infra lead (Angus Meyer) cares about latency/scale; Procurement (Priya Rao) driving contract terms; Product (Samir) owns fallback model acceptance tests.
Next POC iteration: run targeted warm-pool test with 4 pre-warmed GPUs + predictive autoscaler for 72h (scheduled 2026-03-15). Deliverables: updated perf report, cost model, and draft SLA term sheet.

Quotes/feedback from call: 'If warm pools save us 0.3% p99 we keep conversion — willing to pay a premium for predictable latency' — CTO. 'We need clear crediting if p99 breaches happen during peak windows' — Procurement.

Open technical questions: 1) exact cold-start time for model variants (float16 vs 4-bit quantized), 2) recommended batch sizing algorithm for mixed rerank/generation workload, 3) can Redwood expose per-GPU headroom metrics for autoscaler tuning.
